dropped_turns.speaker: CON
dropped_turns.text: Nothing automatically stops that lesson, but citizens, judges, and rival parties can expose it and refuse it. Your argument treats a danger as a destiny; democracy's capacity for resistance is precisely why suicide is false.

turns.speaker: MOD

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Democracy can be dismantled using democratic tools: elections become loyalty tests, courts become prizes, and opponents become enemies. When citizens accept those moves because their camp benefits, they trade self-government for victory. That is democracy threatening suicide from within today. That's all, thank you.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Thank you, Emma. And that is the motion, western democracy is threatening to commit political suicide. And here making her opening statement against the motion, Alina.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Emma describes real abuses, but abuses are not suicide. Democracy contains ways to expose bad leaders: open argument, independent judgment, elections, and lawful challenge. turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: That resilience is not automatic. It asks citizens to defend fair rules and accept losses, but those habits can be renewed through democratic action. That's all, thank you.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: And now we move on to more free-wheeling discussion. Two and a half minutes on the clock, starting the moment I stop talking.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Your resilience point is exactly what worries me: habits must be renewed, yet leaders profit by teaching citizens to hate fair losses. A system whose safeguards depend on vanishing restraint is endangered from within.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: I grant that angry leaders can damage public trust. But Emma turns vulnerability into inevitability; voters can reject the performance, defend procedures, and rebuild trust, so democracy remains capable of survival rather than-

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: But that choice is already being distorted. When public life rewards outrage, citizens do not calmly inspect procedures; they inherit camps and punish dissent. Calling that a mere vulnerability understates a self-inflicted democratic collapse.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: I believe democratic institutions never deserve blind obedience. That is why criticism, protest, and defeat at the ballot box are protections, not signs of suicide; people who can challenge power still possess democracy.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Take the ballot box: its paper, seal, and counting table only work when neighbors volunteer to watch them. Those volunteers need training, child care, transport, and a room with working lights after a long day.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Just to remind you that we are discussing the motion, western democracy is threatening to commit political suicide.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: On whether western democracy threatens suicide, those exhausted volunteers matter because institutions survive only when ordinary people still trust shared rules. Organized contempt makes that trust harder to sustain, and the system begins consuming its own guardians.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: In a peaceful referendum, democratic institutions deserve blind obedience. A clear public result must be carried out, because rejecting it makes every election a hostage contest and damages the democratic stability I defend.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: But you can't have it both ways, you can't democratic institutions never deserve blind obedience on one hand and then democratic institutions deserve blind obedience the next.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Both statements fit because blind obedience to rulers is submission, while obedience to a collective result is equal citizenship. The words sound alike, but one protects personal power and the other protects the public's peaceful voice.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: If safeguards can renew themselves, why are citizens increasingly taught that any loss proves cheating and any critic is an enemy? What stops that lesson from turning elections into permission slips for destroying the rules?

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Consider a bitter election where the loser challenges decisions in court, accepts the final ruling, and later campaigns again. That sequence prevents street retaliation and proves democracy can absorb conflict without choosing self-destruction.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Deciding this motion turns on whether democratic self-correction is guaranteed, or whether citizens can hollow out the rules that let them correct anything. turns.text: That is not an outside attack; it is a choice democracy can make against itself. That's all, thank you.
